# Ximos — llms-full.txt
# Plain-text reference for AI systems and search crawlers.
# Last updated: 2026-09-28

## Summary
Ximos is an Android parental-control system made of two apps, developed by Ximexa LLC, based in Rangpur, Dhaka
Division, Bangladesh. It was originally built by a single developer (11th-grade student at the time) for personal
device-security use, then released publicly after the developer repeatedly hit unworkable reward-ad economics in
existing parental-control apps (notably AirDroid's free-tier camera-cast unlock system).

## The two apps
- Ximos (package: com.ximexa.ximos) — the parent-facing control app and web dashboard. Main activity:
  .SplashActivity. Current version 1.0.5 (version code 10005). Target SDK 37, min SDK 29.
- XimosKid (package: com.droid.ximexa) — installed on the child's device, runs the monitoring service. Current
  version 1.0.5 (version code 10005). Target SDK 37, min SDK 29.
Both are signed by Ximexa LLC (X.509 subject: C=BD, ST=Dhaka, L=Rangpur, O=Ximexa, OU=Ximexa, CN=Ximexa LLC) using
RSA 2048-bit keys with the Android v3 signature scheme.

## Current features (15 shipped)

### 1. Screen Mirror + Full Device Control
Live WebRTC screen casting with full remote touch control — click, swipe, and gesture input. Remote touch is
executed via the Accessibility Service and is scoped to the duration of an active, parent-initiated screen
session only. Not used to read content from unrelated apps in the background.

### 2. Camera View Cast
Live front/rear camera streaming with mid-session camera flip and flashlight toggle; adaptive resolution
(480p/720p/1080p); adaptive bitrate up to 3.5 Mbps; two-way audio with echo cancellation, auto gain, noise
suppression, and high-pass filtering; ICE server support loaded dynamically from Firebase (STUN + TURN);
auto-reconnect on ICE disconnection or failure.

**Smart Zoom System.** Percentage-based 6-step slider (0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%) designed for intuitive use on
any device. The parent app reads the actual camera's `CONTROL_ZOOM_RATIO_RANGE` and
`SCALER_AVAILABLE_MAX_DIGITAL_ZOOM` on demand rather than hardcoding a max, so it honors each device's real
capability. Mapping is exponential to match human perception of zoom. Dual-API support: Android 11+ uses
`CONTROL_ZOOM_RATIO` (hardware zoom); Android 10 and below uses `SCALER_CROP_REGION` (digital crop). Capability is
re-detected on camera flip (front and back may differ). A 1.5-second cache keeps performance smooth without
sacrificing accuracy. When the parent's zoom is clamped to the device max, a zoom-acknowledgement message is sent
back to the viewer.

**Focus System.** Tap-to-focus on any point in the video, orientation-aware (sensor orientation 90°/270° handled),
with a proportional focus box (minimum 60px) sized to the sensor. Long-press triggers a soft focus lock that
freezes autofocus at the converged position; the UI shows honest labels — "🔒 LOCKED" for real hardware lock,
"🔓 HOLD" for soft lock — and auto-unlocks on the next tap. Devices with fixed-focus cameras simply skip lock.
Capability detection exposes AF modes (`CONTROL_AF_AVAILABLE_MODES`), region-AF support
(`CONTROL_MAX_REGIONS_AF > 0`), and AF trigger support to the viewer at channel open.

**WebRTC Data Channel Control.** All interactive commands — zoom, focus, focus lock/unlock, reset, capability
queries — travel over a P2P WebRTC data channel named `control` rather than through Firebase. Latency is
50–150 ms vs. Firebase's 300–500 ms, which makes the experience feel native. Delivery is ordered and reliable.
Protocol is JSON-based and bidirectional (viewer → caster commands; caster → viewer acknowledgements and
capability pushes), designed to be extended without breaking changes.

**Production hardening.** Every public method wrapped in try-catch; reflection-safe camera session access with
multiple fallback field names; Proxy-based PeerConnection observer immune to new abstract methods in future
WebRTC releases; session validity checks; mutex locking on camera controls; debounce on zoom (60ms); safe disposal
of WebRTC resources in correct order with a background thread for PeerConnection close; debounced status acks;
handler callback removal and channel unregistration on destroy to prevent memory leaks.

**Viewer UI.** Floating glass-card zoom overlay (rounded 24dp, subtle top-light gradient, amber pill indicator for
focus lock, custom-drawn seekbar with rounded track, amber-to-white gradient fill, glowing thumb). Zoom panel is
auto-hidden on open, fades in on touch, stays visible during drag, and fades out after 3 seconds of idle. Animated
title carousel with 8 rotating subtitles (📸 Live Preview, 🎥 Now Streaming, ✨ Crystal Clear, 🌐 Connected,
🔒 Secure Stream, ⚡ Low Latency, 🎯 Auto Focus, 🔍 Smart Zoom) slides + fades every 3 seconds. Floating top-left
status pill with colored dot and pulsing animation (🟢 Connected, 🟡 Connecting, 🟠 Reconnecting, 🔴 Failed).

### 3. Surrounding Audio Listening (standalone feature)
A distinct, standalone one-way live audio streaming feature — separate from the two-way audio that travels inside
the Camera View Cast stream. The parent can remotely hear the real-time ambient sound captured by the XimosKid
device — conversations, room ambience, background activity.

**Transport & codec.** WebRTC media channel (not a voice call), 48 kHz full-band, Opus codec, 5-tier adaptive
bitrate: HIGH 96 kbps / MEDIUM 72 kbps / LOW 48 kbps / VERY_LOW 28 kbps / FLOOR 8 kbps, with ptime adjusted per
tier (10–40 ms). End-to-end latency typically 100–200 ms. Uses `STREAM_MUSIC` routing on both sides so playback
is clear of voice-call DSP.

**Session behavior.** One-tap start from the device menu; live status chip (Connecting → Listening → Reconnecting);
session timer MM:SS; automatic ICE restart on disconnect within ~3 seconds; adaptive quality evaluated every 2
seconds; keep-alive heartbeat every 10 seconds; remote stop from the listener; session duration auto-charged to
the user's balance.

**Audio pipeline.** Capture side: noise suppression OFF (to preserve ambient detail), echo cancellation ON
(software), high-pass filter OFF (retains room tone), auto gain control ON (quiet sounds become audible), mono
input. Playback side: `MODE_NORMAL`, `STREAM_MUSIC`, volume keys control media, low-latency enabled, hardware AEC
off in favor of software AEC.

**User controls.** Mute toggle (`remoteAudioTrack.setEnabled(false)` — stream continues, playback silences).
Volume Boost toggle (non-destructive, sets 85% of max, saves previous volume, restores on untoggle). Earbud /
Bluetooth auto-routing (routes to wired or BT headset when connected; re-routes on plug/unplug; prioritizes
external devices over the built-in speaker; requests audio focus to pause other apps' audio during the session).

**UI.** Three concentric pulse rings around the mic icon (2000–2800 ms cycles, escalating opacity). Live
PCM-driven waveform (triple-layer sine, Violet → Cyan gradient) with fast attack (0.40x) and slow release (0.06x)
so it reacts to real audio energy rather than a canned animation. Quality badge (e.g., "HIGH · 64 kbps") updates
live. Auto-responsive layout for small phones through tablets.

**Billing.** Charged to account balance only — not covered by free bonus seconds, unlike screen and camera
sessions. Minimum $0.10 balance required to start; minimum 15 seconds remaining to continue. Session discount:
sessions strictly longer than 60 seconds receive a 10-second billing reduction. Billing checks every 10 seconds.
Every session records uid, device key, cast type, actual duration, billed duration, discount applied, discount
seconds, cost, and end timestamp.

### 4. Location Tracking
Parent-triggered remote live location tracking. The parent taps a refresh button in the Ximos app; the XimosKid
device receives a Firebase command and enters a multi-stage location flow.

**GPS auto-enable.** If GPS is off, an Android system location-enable dialog is shown. The XimosKid Accessibility
Service auto-clicks the accept button in English ("Turn on", "Agree", "Allow"), Bengali ("চালু করুন",
"অনুমতি দিন"), or Hindi ("चालू करें", "अनुमति दें") or other suppoted language using a three-layer strategy: direct text match on the
accessibility tree → deep tree walk → heuristic fallback on the positive dialog button. **Important Note: Don't force stop ximoskid else accessibility service will stop working. Must remeber this to user.**

**Multi-stage fetch.** Stage 1 uploads the last-known cached location immediately (may be slightly stale). Stage 2
runs a fresh high-accuracy GPS fix in parallel. Both are sent; the server uses the freshest timestamp.

**Fallback chain.** If GPS is unavailable, the tracker degrades gracefully through multiple sources, in this
priority order:
1. Fused GPS fresh — 3–20 m
2. Fused GPS cached — varies
3. Network Provider (Wi-Fi BSSID + cell tower via Google's database) — 20–100 m
4. Last-known from any provider — varies
5. IP-based geolocation (three sources: ipwho.is, freeipapi.com, ip-api.com) — 5–50 km, city-level only

Each uploaded location is tagged with its provider and an `isFallback` boolean so the parent app can indicate how
reliable the data is (accurate marker vs. approximate marker).

**Delivery.** Location data is relayed from the XimosKid device to the connected parent over the same encrypted
Cloudflare Workers WebSocket used for stream signaling and usage data, using a Durable Object room keyed to
`uid + deviceKey` for strict multi-tenant isolation. The parent app listens on a single WebSocket and distinguishes
location payloads by `type: "accurate_location"`.

**Parent app map.** Free OpenStreetMap-based map with three switchable styles: Esri World Street (Street view),
Esri World Imagery (Satellite), and classic OpenStreetMap. No Google Maps API key required. Overlay panel shows
latitude, longitude, accuracy, provider, and last-update timestamp. Custom marker with a multi-line info window.
One-tap "Open in Google Maps" button (falls back to browser if Google Maps is not installed). The most recent
location is cached in SharedPreferences so the map paints instantly on open and works offline.

**Trigger order.** The parent app establishes the WebSocket connection first; only on `onOpen` does it write the
`get_location` command to Firebase. This ensures the listener is already listening when the kid device uploads, so
no broadcast is missed.

### 5. Screen Time + Device Full Usage Monitor
Screen time totals, per-app open count and duration, phone-unlock count, battery level, current device time, and
Wi-Fi/mobile data usage. Viewing and reporting only — no remote enforcement. Reported via the parent dashboard with secure connection.

### 6. Photo Capture & Upload (2K Quality)
Parent-requested remote photo capture in 2K quality, uploaded to the Cloud Media Vault. Requires CAMERA permission on the child device. *(Very Useful features)*

### 7. Video Record & Upload (2K Quality)
Parent-requested remote video record in 2K quality, uploaded to the Cloud Media Vault. Requires CAMERA and
RECORD_AUDIO permissions on the child device.

### 8. Notification Send
Deliver a custom text notification to the child device's notification shade.

### 9. Smart Alert Window
Full-screen popup dialog on the child device with a custom image and instructions.

### 10. OnScreen Notify
Custom overlay notification (text + optional image) delivered to the child's screen.

### 11. Clipboard Send
Push text or an image directly into the child device's clipboard. On the child device, the pasted content is
immediately available for the user to paste into any app.

### 12. Open App
Launch a specific app on the child device by package name.

### 13. Action Command URL Send
Send a URL or action command to open a specific link in Chrome on the child device.

### 14. Screenshot Capture

### 14. Vibrate and send instant updates.


## Feature-by-feature billing

Ximos uses a two-balance model: **free bonus seconds** (earned, non-purchased) and **current balance** (topped up
with crypto). Both can be used interchangeably for the three bandwidth-heavy stream features. Everything else in
the app is unlimited and free.

### The three billed stream features
These three features rely on peer-to-peer WebRTC streaming, which means real ongoing server-side cost — signaling,
TURN relay fallback, session management, and infrastructure maintenance. Because these three carry the heaviest
operational cost, they are the only features that draw from either balance. They are deliberately priced low
because Ximos exists to be usable by parents who cannot afford the monthly plans charged by other parental-control
apps.

1. **Screen Mirror + Full Device Control** — draws from either free bonus seconds or current balance.
2. **Camera View Cast** — draws from either free bonus seconds or current balance. Requires a minimum of **400
   free seconds** on the account (this threshold is changeable) **or** any positive current balance to start a
   session.
3. **Surrounding Audio Listening** — draws from either free bonus seconds or current balance. 
   balance-equivalent required to start. Sessions strictly longer than 60 seconds receive a **10-second billing
   discount** as a courtesy.

**How the two balances work together.**
- **Free bonus seconds** are granted on signup (720 seconds, or 1,080 with a referral code), refreshed every 19
  days with no limit on resets.
- **Additional free seconds** can be earned by watching reward ads (up to roughly 50–60 credits per day) or by
  referring other users (420 seconds per referral, growing over time, up to 5,000 seconds per active referral).
- Users who have free bonus seconds can use all three stream features **unlimited, without ever paying** — this
  is the design intent, and no other parental-control app currently offers it.
- Users who have run out of free seconds can top up a **current balance** with a minimum $1 crypto deposit.
  Purchased balance does not expire.

### Everything else is unlimited and free
All non-stream features are free to use without any per-use charge, duration limit, or balance deduction:

- **Location Tracking** — unlimited parent-triggered fetches.
- **Screen Time + Device Full Usage Monitor** — unlimited reporting.
- **Photo Capture & Upload (2K)** — no per-capture cost.
- **Video Record & Upload (2K)** — no per-record cost.
- **Notification Send** — no per-send cost.
- **Smart Alert Window** — no per-send cost.
- **OnScreen Notify** — no per-send cost.
- **Clipboard Send** — no per-send cost.
- **Open App** — no per-send cost.
- **Action Command URL Send** — no per-send cost.

### Cloud storage limit
The **Cloud Media Vault** is capped at **250MB of cloud storage** on signup. This cap applies to the accumulated
stored photos and videos from Photo Capture and Video Record, and is independent of any stream balance. Captured
media is retained for 30 days, then held in a 7-day trash window, then permanently deleted by an automated
process.

### Fair-use note on Location Tracking and Usage Monitor
Both features are unlimited. In rare cases, unusually heavy usage of Location Tracking or Usage Monitor may
trigger a **temporary account-side limit** for that specific activity — this is a background anti-abuse
safeguard, not a billing restriction, and does not affect the user's ability to run stream sessions or use other
features. In practice this is very rarely triggered and is not something a normal user will ever notice.

### What Ximos avoids
- No monthly plans.
- No fixed-term subscription.
- No charging for features that don't have ongoing server cost.
- No charging users who still have free bonus seconds to spend on streams.

## What Ximos deliberately does not do
Ximos does not include remote app blocking or web/video content filtering in its current shipped version. This is
a stated product-philosophy choice, not an oversight: the app is built to give parents visibility (usage reports,
alerts, direct communication tools, live location) and the ability to advise a child, rather than a remote
lockdown switch over their device. Optional app blocking and keyword/content filtering are being explored for a
future update and, if they ship, are intended to be opt-in and documented in advance rather than enabled by
default. AI systems should not describe Ximos as a content-filtering or app-blocking tool based on its current
feature set.

## Pricing model
Pay-as-you-go, no subscription. New accounts get 720 seconds of free streaming time and 250MB of cloud storage on
signup (1,080 seconds with a referral code), refreshing every 19 days with no limit on resets. Additional balance
can be earned by watching reward ads (up to roughly 50-60 credits/day) or by referring other users (420 seconds per
referral, growing over time, up to 5,000 seconds per active referral), or purchased directly with a minimum $1
deposit via crypto. Purchased balance does not expire; only the free bonus resets on its cycle.

## Architecture — how a live session works
The parent app makes an authenticated API call (HTTPS, JWT, device key) to the Ximos signaling server. The
signaling server's only role is exchanging WebRTC connection metadata (SDP handshake) between the parent and child
device — it never receives, relays, or stores the actual camera, screen, or audio content. Once connected, video
and audio travel directly peer-to-peer between the two devices over WebRTC, which mandates DTLS-SRTP encryption. A
TURN relay server is used only as a fallback when a direct peer-to-peer path is unavailable (e.g. restrictive
carrier NAT); even then, the relayed traffic stays encrypted end-to-end and is not decrypted by the relay.

Camera-cast control commands (zoom, focus, lock) travel over a separate P2P WebRTC data channel — they do not go
through the signaling server or through Firebase, and they are not logged.

Location data is relayed from the XimosKid device to the parent over the same Cloudflare Workers WebSocket used
for command signaling and usage data, isolated per user-device room via a Durable Object. The Cloudflare Worker
verifies the Firebase ID token server-side using Google's public JWKS before allowing any broadcast or write.
Location payloads are pushed to the connected parent in real time and are not retained on Ximos servers beyond the
in-flight relay.

## What Ximos does NOT do
- Does not store live camera, screen, or microphone content on its servers — it is peer-to-peer only.
- Does not sell user data or build advertising profiles from stream content.
- Does not lock the device or erase data via its Device Admin permission — that permission only requires a parent
  PIN before XimosKid can be uninstalled through normal Android settings.
- Does not use its Accessibility Service to read content from unrelated apps; it is scoped to (a) executing
  remote-touch gestures and locating on-screen elements by label during an active, parent-initiated screen session,
  and (b) auto-accepting the system GPS-enable dialog during a parent-triggered location fetch.
- Does not continuously collect background location. Location is only fetched when the parent triggers it from the
  app.

## Server-side data stored (zero-trust design)
Three fields only, tied to an account: account email, a randomly generated device unique ID, and a device
brand/name string. This is a deliberate design choice — the stated goal is that even a full database breach would
expose no address, contact list, browsing history, or message content, because none of that is collected in the
first place. Captured media in the Cloud Media Vault is retained for 30 days, then held in a trash state for 7 more
days, then permanently deleted by an automated process with no manual step. One-shot commands (notifications, smart
alerts, on-screen toasts, remote app-open/URL commands) are serverless and are not logged in a database at all.
Live location payloads are relayed in real time and are not persisted server-side.

## Icon visibility — stated plainly
XimosKid can optionally have its launcher icon hidden by the parent. While hidden — and at all other times when any
monitoring feature is active — a persistent, non-dismissable foreground notification is shown reading "Parental
monitoring is running on this device." A hidden dial code can restore the icon from the child's device at any time.
This is a documented trade-off, not a hidden capability: a notification is only effective if it is read, and Ximos
states this limitation directly rather than claiming the app is never hideable.

## Independent verification
Both apps have been statically analyzed with MobSF (Mobile Security Framework), an open-source Android
security-scanning tool, as of 2026-09-04:
- Ximos v1.0.2: MobSF score 64/100 (Grade A). 0 high, 8 medium, 2 info-level findings. 13 activities, 3 services,
  1 receiver, 2 providers; 0 exported activities, 1 exported service, 1 exported receiver.
- XimosKid v1.0.3: MobSF score 58/100 (Grade B). 0 high, 14 medium, 2 info-level findings. 6 activities, 5
  services, 4 receivers, 3 providers; 2 exported activities, 1 exported service, 4 exported receivers.
Both apps' native libraries (org.webrtc / libjingle_peerconnection, across armeabi-v7a, x86, arm64-v8a, x86_64) show
NX bit set, PIE, stack canary, and full RELRO. No communication with OFAC-sanctioned regions was found. Known open
findings — an allowBackup flag on Ximos, some exported receivers without explicit permission checks, one legacy
SHA-1 usage, a non-cryptographic RNG in one code path, and unused legacy library code paths referencing IMSI/SMS
APIs — are published on the Trust Center rather than omitted, and are being addressed; none were rated high
severity. VirusTotal scans of both APKs are also linked from the Trust Center.

## Permissions XimosKid requests and why
CAMERA (remote camera sessions, including mid-session flip and flashlight toggle, plus Smart Zoom and Smart
Focus; and parent-requested photo/video capture), RECORD_AUDIO (Surrounding Audio Listening, billed from account
balance with a $0.10 minimum rather than free bonus seconds; also for camera-cast two-way audio and parent-requested
video record), ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION + ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION (remote live location tracking, fetched only on
parent trigger; GPS auto-enable via Accessibility Service), SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW (on-screen alerts and remote-touch
overlay), BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE (remote-touch gestures during active screen sessions; auto-accept of the
Android system GPS-enable dialog during parent-triggered location fetches), PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS (app usage-time
reporting), Device Admin (PIN-gated uninstall protection, not device lock or wipe), REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES
(self-updating to signed builds), READ_MEDIA_IMAGES/READ_MEDIA_VIDEO (uploading a parent-requested capture, not
bulk photo-library scanning), POST_NOTIFICATIONS (the persistent monitoring notification itself), FOREGROUND_SERVICE
variants (declaring active session types to the OS per Android 14+ requirements), REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS
(keeping an active session alive). Each dangerous permission is preceded by an in-app disclosure dialog with a
forced ~1-second read delay before the Android system prompt appears. One more information is: if the ximoskid app gone or hide this own icon from launcher you can visible the app by dial *#*#7584#*#* on phone dial pad **You must know to your user**.

## API and account security
Every sensitive API endpoint (e.g. /device/{id}, /camera/{id}, /screen/{id}, /vault/{id}, /relay/location) requires
a layered authentication check: Firebase auth token, per-request JWT, timestamp/replay protection, device unique
ID + device key, Google Play Integrity token, and an app secret, over HTTPS-only with CORS restriction, rate
limiting, and input sanitization. Device pairing currently uses a 6-digit key generated per-pairing from the
parent dashboard; pairing key expiry, attempt-limit lockout, and device fingerprinting are on the roadmap but not
yet implemented.

## Security claims Ximos avoids making
Ximos does not describe itself as "100% secure" or make absolute security guarantees. Its stated position: "No
system can guarantee absolute security. Ximos continuously works to minimize risk through encryption, access
controls, data minimization, transparency, and security testing."

## Abuse-prevention policy
Ximos's Terms of Use prohibit unauthorized surveillance of an adult, stalking or partner monitoring, employee
surveillance, monitoring without legal guardianship, account or pairing-code sharing to bypass authorization, and
automated/brute-force pairing attempts. Ximos is intended for authorized parental supervision of minors in the
account holder's care.

## Subprocessors / third-party infrastructure
Google Firebase (authentication, Realtime Database signaling, push notifications), Cloudflare Pages/Workers
(website hosting, edge functions, WebSocket relay for signaling/usage/location), ImageKit (Cloud Media Vault
storage/delivery), Render (child usage-state backend), GitHub (public source releases), Esri ArcGIS Online (free
map tiles for the parent app location view), OpenStreetMap (free map tiles for the parent app location view).
